chunks: 9-13 Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taliqani, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us; he said: al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sukkari narrated to us; he said: Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Jawhari narrated to us, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Imarah, from his father, from Abu ‘Abd Allah Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله married fifteen women, and he consummated marriage with thirteen of them, and he passed away while nine remained. As for the two with whom he did not consummate marriage, they were ‘Amrah and al-Sanā. As for the thirteen with whom he consummated marriage, the first of them was Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, then Sawrah bint Zam‘ah, then Umm Salamah, whose name was Hind bint Abi Umayyah, then Umm ‘Abd Allah ‘A’ishah bint Abi Bakr, then Hafsah bint ‘Umar, then Zaynab bint Khuzaymah ibn al-Harith, Umm al-Masakin, then Zaynab bint Jahsh, then Umm Habibah Ramlah bint Abi Sufyan, then Maymunah bint al-Harith, then Zaynab bint ‘Umays, then Juwayriyah bint al-Harith, then Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab.

And the one who offered herself to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was Khawlah bint Hakim al-Sulami. He also had two concubines for whom he apportioned time along with his wives: Mariyah and Rayhanah al-Khandaqiyyah. And the nine from whom he passed away were: ‘A’ishah, Hafsah, Umm Salamah, Zaynab bint Jahsh, Maymunah bint al-Harith, Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Juwayriyah bint al-Harith, and Sawrah bint Zam‘ah.
And the best of them was Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, then Umm Salamah bint al-Harith.

key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله

ai.seo_question: How many wives did the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله have, and who were they according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a biographical listing of the wives of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, noting how many he married, with whom marriage was consummated, and which wives remained at the time of his passing. It concludes by identifying Khadijah bint Khuwaylid and then Umm Salamah as the most excellent among them.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 9-13 Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taleqani - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Al-Hussein ibn Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sokri quoted Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Juwhary, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Ammarat, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aba Abdullah Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), “

God’s Prophet (MGB) married fifteen women, and consummated the marriage with thirteen of them. He (MGB) had nine wives when he (MGB) died. The two with whom he had not slept with were Omra and Sina . The thirteen wives with whom he (MGB) consummated his marriage were: first Khadijah - the daughter of Khuwaylid ; second Sorat - the daughter of Zam’a ; third Umma Salma whose name was Hind - the daughter of Abi Umayya ; fourth Umma Abdullah Ayesha - the daughter of Abu Bakr; fifth Hafsah - the daughter of Umar ; sixth Zaynab - the daughter of Khuzayma ibn al-Harith - Umma al-Masakin ; seventh Zaynab - the daughter of Jahsh ; eighth Umma Habiba Ramlat - the daughter of Abu Sufyan ; ninth Maymuna - the daughter of Al-Harith ; tenth Zaynab - the daughter of Amees; eleventh Jowayreeyat - the daughter of Al-Harith ; twelfth Safiyya - the daughter of Huyayy ibn Akhtab.

And the wife who had devoted herself to the Prophet (MGB) was Khule - the daughter of Hakim al-Salmy. He (MGB) also had two slave-wives called Maryam Qibtiyah and Rayhana al-Khandaqiya with whom he took turns sleeping every so many nights just like his other wives. And the nine who were still alive when he (MGB) died were: Ayesha; Hafsah; Umma Salma; Zaynab - the daughter of Jahsh; Maymuna - the daughter of Al-Harith; Umma Habiba - the daughter of Abu Sufyan; Safiyya - the daughter of Huyayy ibn Akhtab; Jowayreeyat - the daughter of Al-Harith and Sorat - the daughter of Zam’a.
Their noblest one was Khadijah - the daughter of Khuwaylid . Then the next noble one was Umma Salma - the daughter of Al-Harith.”
